name: Platt's Lane Estates apartments, 532–534
summary: Two offset three-storey walk-ups feature paired columns of narrow window openings in the west gable and a chimneystack on the western ridge. Access is from the parking side.

evidence.note: Three rows of two narrow punched openings and small vent pairs appear in the brown gable.
The north roof slope, projecting balconies and a capped chimney are visible above the eaves.

Two zigzag wings above south parking with parallel ridges and one west ridge flue, with a medium brown roof colour from a 7 by 7 pixel sample in 2025 aerial-source.jpg centered at (452, 176) measuring #6c5a4b.

Regional-2m LiDAR gives a P50 of 10.14 m, P90 of 11.06 m, and maximum of 13.57 m, indicating a three-storey apartment roofline near 11.1 m while the higher maximum likely reflects the west ridge flue or adjacent foliage.
The City's geocoded address points confirm the street addresses and three-storey height for the apartment buildings.
Western Facilities Management estate aerial photograph.
Western Housing, 1976 walk-up apartment and townhouse development.
Same-estate apartment material samples from frame 130394331 measure fluted block at (98.5%, 49%) as #88725b and smooth buff panel at (92.6%, 48.2%) as #d2ba98.
Comparable photographed adjacent apartment buildings on the estate supply details for unseen walls, estimated door and window bay sizes, and balcony canopy and ledge materials.

Frame 46920578 shows brown porch-height opaque masonry screens below balcony stacks on the estate apartment, and frame 130394407 shows two closely spaced narrow openings per floor about 3.2 m centre-to-centre on 532–534's west gable.
City of London building footprint compared with the 2025 orthophoto to locate individual gabled wings and grounded patio screens, while balcony and entrance placement on hidden walls is inferred.

Cross-sections of the 1 m return grid show paired gable slopes near one in three. Local fits set the ridge and eaves of each narrow and wide roof section independently; the orthophoto shows the balcony stack positions.

notes: Alternating roof widths create shallow re-entrant corners for the brown balcony stacks. Balcony railing tops, window frames, eave trim and ridge vents differ in material. Partly concealed entrances and patio details are approximate.
